_comment: 🧩️ This subset's own contribution. Wave F registers the two third-party reproductions of its first inferences, `🪜️storey-levels` and `🧱️wall-layout`: shapely 2 (GEOS) audits wall axes and footprints, IfcOpenShell 0.8.4.post1 measures straight walls with its geometry kernel. The host packages both adapters import are declared one level up, in the plugin's own 🔮️oracles/🔣️.json. Later waves APPEND their oracles, mutation catalogs and manifests here.

oracles.rationale: Shapely 2 over GEOS is the reference planar geometry library. A wall axis becomes a real LineString (an arc is sampled into 4096 chords) and shapely, not this repository, measures the join-trimmed footprint polygons, the face lengths and the join invariants of the committed wall-layout table: every straight corner is re-derived from GEOS offset_curve carriers, joined footprints must not overlap, a cross overlaps by exactly its committed area, a two-wall node covers the area of LineString.buffer(join_style=mitre) and a butt equals its band minus the body of the wall it butts against. The same oracle proves the parametric law as a metamorphic property. Storey elevations are a running sum that no third-party engine owns, so they are pinned by math.fsum against the subject's f64 sum, by the parametric law, and by the kernel z-extents of the sibling ifcopenshell case. The solids case re-derives the volume and bounds of every planar column, beam, slab, roof, stair and railing from the authored snapshot alone with Polygon.area, affinity, mitred buffer, convex_hull, LineString.interpolate and a numpy linear program audited by shapely.ops.polylabel. The floor plan (poche, column and mullion areas and outline lengths on real polygons) and the diagnostics (clash overlap areas by polygon intersection, missing ids, level arithmetic) are audited the same way. The views (`view-linework`) are audited the same way: the plane of a section is a LineString whose intersection with the footprint polygons of walls and rotated columns gives the section cut areas, the slab of a view is a polygon intersection, the projection outline of an elevation or section is the unary_union of the extents of the connected pieces along the plane, and the datum lines are clipped to the crop box. The annotations (dimensions, tags, notes, leaders) are audited with offset_curve wall faces, interpolate opening centres and the GEOS distance of two parallel faces, plus the metamorphic laws that lengthening a wall lengthens its end-to-end dimension by the same distance and that moving a column leaves its tag text unchanged.

engine.implementation: Shapely 2 over the GEOS geometry engine

oracles.rationale: IfcOpenShell is the reference open-source IFC implementation and ships its own C++ geometry kernel. Every straight wall of the committed layout is written as an IfcWall whose body is its committed join-trimmed footprint extruded by its height (IfcArbitraryClosedProfileDef), placed at its committed base z; the walls of the element-solids cases additionally get one IfcOpeningElement per window, door and void (IfcRelVoidsElement) so that the kernel's boolean subtracts them. The model is serialised to ISO 10303-21 text, re-opened and tessellated; the measured z extent and volume of the triangulation must equal the committed base_z, top_z and volume. The same engine validates the IFC export and its quantities in the IO wave.

three.js is the renderer the editor and viewer meshes are ultimately drawn with, written by unrelated authors. Every element solid of the walls, curtain walls and window and door fillers is committed as a blessed mesh next to its authored snapshot; this oracle loads each mesh as a BufferGeometry and measures volume (the signed sum of tetrahedra with three's Vector3 dot and cross, three ships no volume function), surface area (Triangle.getArea), bounds (Box3.setFromBufferAttribute) and the triangle count, and the subject reports the same numbers from its live element-solids inference. Adapter at ../🧪️tests/🎲️infer-bim-1-solids-three/🟦️.ts.

engine.implementation: three.js BufferGeometry / Triangle / Box3 over the bun runtime

oracles.rationale: IfcOpenShell is the reference open-source IFC implementation, written by unrelated authors, and ships its own C++ geometry kernel. It opens the committed IFC 2x3 export of the BIM house (a file the subject wrote with its own Part-21 writer), checks that the file parses and declares IFC2X3, counts the entities of every class the export writes, reads the spatial containment of every product, and tessellates every straight wall, level slab, column and beam with its kernel (openings are subtracted through IfcRelVoidsElement). The kernel volumes must equal the written base quantities and the subject's report.

IfcOpenShell is the reference open-source IFC implementation, written by unrelated authors, and ships its own C++ geometry kernel and the IFC4 EXPRESS schema with every WHERE rule. It opens the committed IFC4 (ADD2 TC1) exports of the BIM models (files the subject wrote with its own Part-21 writer), validates every attribute type and rule, counts the entities of every class the export writes, reads the spatial containment, the window and door types with their operation, the property set templates, the classification chains and the type property sets, and tessellates every straight wall, slab, column, beam and covering with its kernel. The kernel volumes must equal the written base quantities and the subject's report.

three.js is the reference WebGL scene graph, written by unrelated authors. Its GLTFLoader parses the committed binary glTF export of the BIM house (a file the subject wrote with its own GLB container writer): it checks the container framing and the JSON, reads the accessors and index buffers, composes the node transforms and builds the scene graph. The oracle counts the nodes, meshes, primitives, triangles and materials, the element nodes per kind and per storey (node extras surface as userData) and measures the world bounds of every vertex through the whole site, building and storey chain with Box3.setFromObject(scene, true).

engine.implementation: three.js GLTFLoader scene graph over the bun runtime

oracles.rationale: lxml (libxml2) is a namespace-aware XML parser written by unrelated authors, and shapely (GEOS) is the reference computational-geometry library. lxml opens the committed SVG export of the BIM house (a file the subject wrote with its own XML writer), requires the SVG 1.1 root with a millimetre size equal to its viewBox, finds the storey groups and counts their regions, lines, texts, style classes and arc commands. An own SVG path reader feeds shapely, which measures the even-odd area of the straight cut poche regions and the length of the straight lines per style, converted from paper millimetres to model metres at 1:100. Arcs are sampled for an audit value only.

engine.implementation: lxml 6.1.3 (libxml2) XML parser with shapely 2.1.2 (GEOS) geometry

oracles.rationale: pypdf is a pure-Python PDF reader written by unrelated authors. It opens the committed PDF 1.7 sheet set of the BIM room (a file the subject wrote page by page with the stdio PDF document writer), counts the pages, reads every page box and converts it from points to millimetres, and extracts the text of every page with its own content-stream interpreter. The subject reports the same table from the sheet-layout inference: one page per sheet in print order, the paper size of the sheet as it lies and the number, title and project that its title block prints.

packages.role: structurally unrelated second differ, corroborating whether the document moved at all
draft-07 validation of every committed mutation payload against its own leaf schema, and rejection of an undeclared member

oracles.rationale: jsonpatch answers the DIFF, corroborated by deepdiff and jsonschema, and never applies a mutation itself. For every committed quintet (before, mutation, after, typed diff, outcome) it derives an RFC 6902 patch from (before, after) with make_patch, applies it to reproduce the after-snapshot exactly, and holds the typed ModelDiff to it: the records the operations reach are exactly the records the diff declares, classified Created, Deleted or Patched, a Patched entry carries exactly the changed fields at their new values (property sets via the assigned patch), a rejected or no-op row yields no operation. The inverse patch restores the before-snapshot and patch plus inverse sum to the identity. deepdiff, a structurally unrelated algorithm, must agree with jsonpatch about whether the document moved at all. jsonschema validates the payload against the leaf schema and must reject the same payload with an undeclared member. WHAT IT DOES NOT ADJUDICATE: whether a change was the right one, only that the committed diff, payload and snapshots describe each other.

packages.role: GEOS area and perimeter of the section polygons of the family solids and their validity
strongly connected components and topological generations of the parameter dependency graph, inside the independent Python interpreter of the expression framework module

oracles.rationale: numpy rebuilds every solid of a parametric family as explicit facets (divergence-theorem volume, cross-product area, mitered sweeps, revolutions in rings) and shapely measures the section polygons, while the independent Python interpreter of the expression framework module (ast dimension checking, networkx dependency order, Decimal rounding), reached through a Python recursive-descent translator of the formulas, resolves every parameter. None of them has seen this repository's Rust. The oracle audits the closed forms (a prism is its section area times its height, a pipe is pi r^2 h, a revolution obeys Pappus' theorem) and the parametric laws (the order of the parameters changes nothing, widening a table by 0.1 m widens its top by 0.1 m x depth x thickness) before it answers.

engine.implementation: numpy ndarray facets, networkx dependency graphs and shapely (GEOS) polygons over the CPython interpreter of the expression oracle

oracles.rationale: jsonschema (Draft 2020-12) decides whether a property value is allowed by its definition. Every definition of a property set template becomes a JSON Schema (type, minimum, maximum, enum) and the validator, not this repository, answers the findings of the effective properties: a value whose kind tag differs from its definition is a kind mismatch, the first violated keyword of the schema is the range or enumeration issue. The oracle restates the inheritance rules (own value, else the value of the type, else the default of the template) from the authored records alone and audits that every default satisfies its own definition, that an own value has a finding exactly when the validator rejects it, that a required property without a value is reported once and that an inherited value is never re-reported at its instance. WHAT IT DOES NOT ADJUDICATE: whether a template is sensible, only that the derived values and findings follow from the authored records.

lxml (libxml2) is a namespace-aware XML parser written by unrelated authors, shapely (GEOS) is the reference computational-geometry library and numpy evaluates the vector algebra. lxml opens the committed gbXML 7.03 exports of the BIM thermal envelope (files the subject wrote through the stdio XML writer), checks the root, units, xs:ID syntax and uniqueness and that every reference resolves, validates the document with the official XSD when it is committed, and reads every space, zone, surface, opening, construction, layer, material and window type. numpy recomputes the normal, area, azimuth and tilt of every surface from its polygon, shapely lays it into its own plane to check the rectangular geometry, the openings inside it and their positions, and the divergence theorem closes every space (outward area vectors sum to zero, the polygons enclose the stated volume, the floors add up to the stated area). The surfaces are regrouped by space, kind, boundary, neighbour and compass sector and compared with the table of the energy inference oracle. The subject reports the same table from the plan it writes.

engine.implementation: lxml 6.1.3 (libxml2) XML parser with shapely 2.1.2 (GEOS) geometry and numpy vector algebra

oracles.rationale: IfcOpenShell is the reference open-source IFC implementation, written by unrelated authors, and ships the official property set templates of IFC 2x3 and IFC4 (ADD2) and the EXPRESS schemas with every WHERE rule. It opens the committed IFC 2x3 and IFC4 exports of the BIM house (files the subject wrote with its own Part-21 writer), reads the thermal property sets of every product with their IFC value types, checks every derived property against the standard template of its set (the property exists and has the template's primary measure type), restates the rules from the snapshot alone (kelvin set points, air changes from the clear height of the space, type values of windows and doors, ISO 6946 bounds of the layer stacks of walls, slabs and roofs, authored values kept and derived values listed) and runs the EXPRESS rules. The subject reports the same table from its document.
